newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Morgan Stanley Africa cuts bonds, raises equities.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley Africa cuts bonds, raises equities.

text.p: Morgan Stanley's Africa Investment Fund portfolio saw a marked shift away from fixed-income assets towards equities, portfolio manager Jaideep Khanna said on Tuesday.
Speaking at a Societe Generale Frankel Pollak investment conference, Khanna said at the end of 1996, the group's portfolio was 91 percent equities, three percent fixed income and six percent cash.
This compared with a 47-percent exposure in equities, 49 percent in fixed income and four percent in cash at the end of March 1994.
On a country basis, the fund's exposure to South Africa has dropped to 43.8 percent at the end of 1996 from a peak of 69.4 percent at the end of 1994.
The main gainers have been Zimbabwe and Egypt, with Zimbabwe's weighting jumping from 1.1 percent in the last two years to 15.9 percent and Egypt going from zero to 14.1 percent.
